title: One wrong label, five neighbours
hook: The closest example is labelled wrong. Should you trust it, or ask around?

knows: classifying something by what it most resembles
doesNotKnow: how the choice of k handles a mislabelled neighbour

misconception: Looking at only the single closest example is the most accurate way to classify.
objective: The learner can explain that voting among several nearest neighbours outvotes a single bad label, and that too large a k gives every point the overall majority.

claims.text: At the new dot, the single nearest dot is the mislabelled orange one, so k = 1 gives orange; its 5 nearest dots are 4 blue and 1 orange, so k = 5 gives blue (k = 3: 2 blue, 1 orange; k = 7: 6 blue, 1 orange).
claims.source: Fixed layout in Demo.tsx (DOTS, QUERIES[0] = (3.2, 3.0)); Euclidean distances 0.28, 0.72, 1.00, 1.13, 1.17, 1.60, 1.81 to the seven nearest. Reproduced by vote() in Demo.tsx. The layout is invented for the toy.

claims.text: With k = 13 every dot votes (6 blue, 7 orange), so every new dot is labelled orange wherever it sits.
claims.source: When k equals the number of training points the vote is the same for every query: the overall majority class. Toy counts from DOTS in Demo.tsx (the bad label counts as orange).

claims.text: Small k follows noise in the labels; larger k smooths the boundary, and too large a k blurs real boundaries.
claims.source: About real methods: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009, The Elements of Statistical Learning, §2.3.2 and §13.3 (k-nearest-neighbour classifiers, effect of k).

claims.text: A k-nearest-neighbours classifier gives a new point the majority label among its k nearest labelled points.
claims.source: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009, The Elements of Statistical Learning, section 13.3.

recall.question: A photo classifier labels a new photo by its single most similar training photo, and a few training photos are mislabelled. What change makes one bad label matter less?
options: Let the 5 or so most similar photos vote
Use only the most similar photo, but measure similarity more carefully
recall.why: A handful of neighbours outvotes one bad label. Letting every photo vote gives every new photo the most common label, which erases the real differences.
